The building was used by Reynolds Electrical and Engineering Company (REECo), a long-time general contractor that provided extensive support of day-to-day site operations for the Control Point and throughout the NNSS. It was also used by Edgerton, Germeshausen, and Grier, Inc. (EG&G), which provided direct technical support to the national laboratories and the Department of Defense (DOD). Beginning in the 1970s, it was an important staging area and electrical power supply point for the NNSS diagnostic trailer fleet. Its unique location immediately along Mercury Highway in Yucca Pass allowed easy accessibility to the forward areas of the NNSS. Building 06-CP-65 is a one-story 240 × 100 ft. rectangular plan building that is oriented north-south with precast concrete wall panels. A loading dock with electrical power hook-ups runs the length of the east elevation. The high, built-up roof sits on concrete and metal decking and is nearly flat with a very low pitch to accommodate proper drainage. Installed along the length of the roof is heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) equipment. Associated with the building are eight accessory resources: a Building 06-CP-65 Mitigation Page 2 of 4 LR021925-1-MIT loading dock (AR1), a retaining wall (AR2), trailer hook-ups (AR3-AR4), substations (AR5-AR6), a storage boxcar (AR7), and parking lot (AR8). The interior consists of open warehouse space in the northern two-thirds of the building and offices in the southern third. The warehouse space is one large rectangular area that measures 180 ft. long and 100 ft. wide. Modular chain-link fencing is used to divide the interior. Two standalone adjoining offices have been built in the middle of the warehouse space. These two offices are not depicted in a 1969 as-built floor plan (Holmes and Narver) but are shown in a 1990 floor plan (EG&G). There is also a room-sized cold storage cooler on the east wall adjacent to double doors that allow access via the loading dock. The cooler may have held filmic media for EG&G. The only other notable structure is a stationary high- pressure air workstation with a flume hood against the south wall of the open warehouse. This wall serves to separate the warehouse space from the offices. Both the room-sized cold storage cooler and the stationary high-pressure air workstation are denoted on the 1969 as-built floor plan and are part of the original design. Offices in the southern portion of the building are constructed around a U-shaped corridor. In addition to restrooms and a shower room, there are currently 16 offices that vary in size depending on their location around the corridor.
